input.quote: Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year, at reasonable times and upon reasonable notice. Commerce One shall bear all costs and expenses of such inspection.
input.rationale: Section 4.4 is the only audit/inspection right binding us (Corio, as licensee/customer), and it substantially meets the preferred position: inspections are limited to once each calendar year, must be conducted at reasonable times and on reasonable (i.e. advance, announced) notice, must be performed by an independent certified public accountant reasonably acceptable to us, and Commerce One bears all costs unless an underpayment exceeding 5% is found — the preferred cost-shift threshold, better than the 10% fallback. The auditor reviews our books and records only; there is no right of direct or remote access to our systems, so no walk-away issue arises. The only sub-elements short of the preferred wording are that notice is "reasonable" rather than a fixed 30 days and that the auditor's confidentiality is covered by the general NDA under Section 10 rather than expressly in the audit clause; these are minor points noted here rather than redlined.
